Coverage release: full Python closure for uv projects.

**What's new**

- **`uv.lock` support**: projects and workspaces managed with uv now
  contribute their complete resolved dependency closure to the check —
  not just the directly declared packages. Workspace members themselves
  are correctly excluded as first-party code.
- `pyproject.toml` parsing now defers to an adjacent `uv.lock` (as it
  already did for `poetry.lock`) — the lockfile is authoritative.

**Why it matters**

On a real-world uv workspace monorepo this raises Python coverage from
the handful of declared dev-tools to the full transitive closure
(124 packages in our reference project) — which is exactly the surface a
CRA vulnerability assessment has to look at.

As always: only component names, versions and ecosystems leave your
machine. Verify it yourself with `--dry-run`.
